_comment: QUSX v1 conformance fixture manifest. Machine-readable contract for third-party implementers: run each fixture's 'file' through your own XSD + ISO Schematron (+ semantic, for js-only rules) checker and compare the rule ids you observe against 'expectedFailingRules'. Every rule id referenced here MUST exist in test/conformance/rules.json (the same file this manifest and schema/qusx.sch both cite). See README.md in this directory for the full consumption contract and the notes below for two known, deliberate multi-rule couplings.
notes: QUSX-HDR-001 (filename NNN.qusx.xml must encode the same surah as the surah attribute) is scoped to files that are part of a corpus tree (see NORMATIVE-RULES.md: 'Files not matching that pattern are outside the corpus naming convention and reported as such'). Every fixture in this suite except the reused test/fixtures/tradition-warsh*/106.qusx.xml files intentionally lives at a non-corpus path; QUSX-HDR-001 is exempt for all fixtures in this manifest and is never listed in expectedFailingRules here.

QUSX-HDR-002..006 are non-portable (need data/raw/quran-metadata-surah-name.json and data/traditions/ayah-counts.json) and are out of scope for this portable fixture suite; a fixture may incidentally trip QUSX-HDR-006 (declared ayahCount vs. the real canonical count) because these are small hand-written excerpts, not full real surahs -- that is expected and not a suite defect.

QUSX-PIN-004 and QUSX-PIN-005 are checkedBy "js" only (not schematron -- see schema/qusx.sch's own header comment: a stateful 'currently open per axis' machine is deliberately not duplicated in XPath). The reference src/validate.js tracks only ONE currently-open sid per axis; reopening an axis while open (PIN-004) or closing with a mismatched eid (PIN-005) necessarily leaves the true still-open sid without a valid matching close in the same pass, so src/validate.js also reports QUSX-PIN-006 alongside the targeted rule. This is not incidental fixture sloppiness -- it is how the single authoritative js checker for these two rules actually behaves, verified by running node src/validate.js against both fixtures. Their expectedFailingRules lists reflect that ground truth.

A handful of reused test/fixtures/*.qusx.xml files (predating this suite) declare ayahCount="7" (the real Al-Fatihah header) but include only 1-2 ayahs, so they incidentally also trip QUSX-AYH-001 alongside their targeted rule. Per the task's reuse instruction these files are referenced by their existing path rather than being edited or duplicated; the incidental QUSX-AYH-001 finding is listed honestly in expectedFailingRules for those entries. New fixtures created directly for this suite (under test/conformance/fixtures/) declare an ayahCount matching their actual content and do not have this issue.

Fixtures targeting an L1 (QUSX-STR) rule are expected to fail XSD validation. Per CONFORMANCE.md ('Levels are cumulative... a document at level N satisfies every rule at levels 0..N'), a document that is not XSD-valid is not meaningfully evaluated at L2 -- a staged pipeline runs L1 first and only proceeds to Schematron/semantic (L2) checks if L1 passes. expectedFailingRules for L1 fixtures therefore lists only the L1 rule, even where the unstaffed reference src/validate.js (which does not stage) would also report an incidental L2 finding on the same missing/invalid attribute.

fixtures.description: Small, hand-written, structurally complete Hafs Al-Fatihah excerpt (2 ayahs, 4 words) satisfying every portable L0-L2 rule.
Reused fixture: an unclosed <word> element makes the document not well-formed XML.
Reused fixture: root <qusx> carries the attribute "surah" twice.
Reused fixture: surah="200" is outside the valid 1-114 range.
Root tradition="not-a-real-tradition" is not a value of the traditionCode enumeration.
A <footnote> element appears as a direct child of <qusx>, which is not one of the ten allowed element names.
<word id="1"> omits the required "position" attribute.
<juz sid="juz:1" fragment="partial"> uses a fragment value outside whole|start|middle|end.
Reused fixture: <ayah> carries both sid and eid on the same element instead of exactly one.
<juz sid="juz:1"> (an opening pin) omits the required "number" attribute.
Reused fixture: the sid value "1:1:hafs-kufi" is opened twice in the document.

A second <page sid="page:2"> opens while <page sid="page:1"> (same axis) is still open. See manifest notes: the reference js checker also reports PIN-005 and PIN-006 here because it tracks only one currently-open sid per axis.
<ayah eid="1:1:wrong-id"> does not match the open sid "1:1:hafs-kufi". See manifest notes: the mismatched close also leaves the true sid unclosed, so PIN-006 is reported alongside PIN-005.
Reused fixture: <ayah sid="1:1:hafs-kufi"> is opened but never closed before end of document.
<juz eid="juz:1" fragment="whole"> puts fragment on a closing (eid) pin instead of the opening (sid) pin.
Reused fixture: opening ayah numbers are [1, 3], skipping 2 -- not a contiguous 1..N sequence.
Word ids appear as 2 then 1 -- not strictly increasing across the document.
Reused fixture: the second <word> in ayah 1 has position="3" instead of the expected 2.
<ayah tradition="warsh-kfqc"> does not match the root <qusx tradition="hafs-kufi">.
Root declares normalization="NFC" but the <word> text uses a decomposed alef+hamza-above sequence (U+0627 U+0654) instead of the precomposed U+0623, so the text is not NFC.
